confidence_flags: dense multi-room sheet at 1:100 — main perimeter/primary beam grid (rows F/E/D/C/B, columns 1-4) read with high confidence; interior beams that bear on another beam rather than a column (grid2 at row D/C, grid3 at row C) and the small stair-landing bump-out east of grid4 read with moderate confidence; see warnings
warnings: 'B5' (grid2, span E-D-C) and the grid2/grid3 mid-span beam changes at rows D and C are all confirmed to sit exactly ON the named grid (not off-grid) — an earlier close read mistook B5 for an unaligned interior beam; re-zoomed and confirmed it runs precisely at x=grid2 (S-06's ring-beam plan and this sheet's own gridlines agree). D2 and C3 have no footing (S-02) — the beam continuing through them without a support is a beam-bears-on-beam condition, not a missing column; flagged confidence_flags:['bears_on_beam'] on the affected segments per §5.

'B3' at D3-D4 is drawn dashed (under the dashed 'S1' sunken-slab boundary) — recorded as a real beam (per §5 nothing here suggests it is only a reference line; dashing on this sheet consistently marks 'behind/under the stepped slab', not 'not built') but flagged lower confidence since dashed linework is harder to trace precisely at this scale.

Small unlabelled 'BX' notches (two on this sheet, near grid2/row E and grid1/row D) are tiny corner jogs with no printed dimension isolating them from the beam they sit on — not recorded as independent elements (would require inventing an unprinted offset); S-08 does carry a 'BX' rebar detail (0.15x0.30, Ø6@0.20) confirming it is a real minor member, just not independently locatable on this plan.

The 'B2X'/'B3' linework north of row F IS a real beam rectangle and is now recorded: a B3 running along dummy row F' from grid2 to grid4 (5.00m) with a B2X spur at each end dropping the printed 1.00m down to row F. An earlier read dismissed it as a fascia/eave reference line on the grounds that no dimension separated it from row F — wrong: the 1.00 is the first segment of this sheet's own vertical dimension chain, and both spurs carry their own printed 'B2X' marks. The SOA canopy slab west of grid2 in that same strip is still only a slab-type marker.

Row C to row B has exactly one labelled vertical beam in the grid2-4 half of the plan and it sits on GRID 2 (its two ends land on the C2 and B2 columns) — recorded as B2 C2-B2. An earlier read placed this at C4-B4. The building's east edge does run C4 to B4 with columns at both ends, but it carries no printed beam mark on this sheet, so it is not recorded as an element.

The small bump-out east of grid4 (dummy grid 4', between rows D-C) is the stair LANDING platform, confirmed by S-11/S-12 stair sections and the 'B1/B2ที่ระดับชานพัก' ('at landing level') callouts on S-05 — its short columns 'CN' rise only from floor-1 to landing level, not full height (S-09). Recorded as element_type 'column' with grid_refs [D4', C4'].

'BX1' (small ~0.40x0.40 beam per S-08) sits in a 0.60 x 0.60 bump east of grid4 at row B, both offsets locally dimensioned on this sheet. Re-zoomed: the bump starts at grid4 itself, so BX1 runs from grid4 east to the dummy x-line 4" (9.60) along row B, and its flanking 'SX' slab-corner markers sit in the same bump. Note this 0.60 is NOT the stair landing's offset — the landing east of grid4 at rows D-C is 0.50 (dummy 4'), a distinction the earlier read collapsed into a single 9.60 line.

The WEST side carries a second small bump: a 'B4X' spur at row C and another at row B run 0.60m west of grid1 (the 0.60 that opens this sheet's x-dimension chain), closed by a beam on the outer line between them — and it is that OUTER beam the printed 'B2' label sits beside, not the grid1 line. All three are now recorded on dummy x-line 1' (-0.60); the CX strut line that used to hold that name was renamed 1" when this house was converted to house 13's reading-order prime scheme — see the grid master. The beam drawn on grid1 itself between the C1 and B1 columns is kept as well but with its mark flagged as inferred, since only one B2 label is printed in that area.

Slab-type markers (SOA/S1/SO/SX per §10) are room/zone tags, not point beams — recorded with approximate area-style grid_ref rather than an exact grid intersection, consistent with how a slab-type marker is drawn on this sheet.
